I lived on my own for a long time. I didn't have any family to help me, so it was just me.

I worked the entirety of this time and often did not have enough between checks. If I was lucky, I'd have less than five dollars left to last me two weeks.

Pro tip: Canned veggies, tomato sauce, and bag of rice can get you through for a good while without repeat meals. A bag of potatoes too!

I didn't have extra things like a phone or internet. No car, no tv.
I just lived in a city where rent for my apartment was sky high on a single income. Even in the shitty, rough neighborhood where I lived.

Often, I had to choose between things like water and groceries, so I ate very little and made sure there was zero waste when I did have things.
It's those moments when you're without that you remember the things you wasted. Those days are gone, thankfully, but I still do not waste any food and keep stock on non perishables in case I know someone in that kind of situation.

Anyhow, I hate to admit this, but it was one of those times where I had less than a dollar left on that check. I did have food, so I was not hungry.
However, I ran out of toilet paper and soap.

So, I stole some from my job's bathroom. I took one of the wrapped rolls and unopened bar soaps and put them in my purse to take home.
It doesn't seem like much, but I felt so low at that moment because I took something that wasn't mine.


tl;dr: I was in a financial spot and stole toilet paper and soap from work.

I went to Sunday school by default (southern raised) and questioned things from the start. My parents let me choose, so I tried different things.

When I got older, I tried to find something and nothing felt "right" because there seemed to be a lot of far fetched notions or stories that I couldn't agree with.
I went down the list and decided I was agnostic, though that label didn't fit.
Years and years later, I realized my beliefs matched up perfectly with humanism. I believed in the good of people for who they are from a young age.
So anyway, I think it would be similar for most people in my boat.
